cover.headline: AI agents found and exploited a zero-day in about *11 minutes*.
cover.sub: On their own, Amazon says. Five changes from 20 Nov on what to settle before an agent runs, plus two courses.

items.title: Attackers' AI agents found a *zero-day* on their own
items.statLabel: minutes from mapping an app's API to writing files on its server, per Amazon
items.what: A suspected China-nexus operator ran Cairn, an open-source AI pentest framework, against East Asian universities from 8 Sep.
items.why: Amazon spotted it on 10 Sep, when it found the attackers' own Cairn server online with no login. Its advice: automate the response.

items.title: Claude computer use reaches *Team and Enterprise*
items.statLabel: by default. Only an Owner or Primary Owner can switch it on
items.what: In beta from 20 Nov, Claude can see a user's screen and work in the desktop apps they allow, on Mac and Windows.
items.why: Anthropic's guide says there is no sandbox between Claude and a user's apps. Write the app allow list before you switch it on.

items.title: Signal now blocks AI from *reading its screen*
items.statLabel: by default: Block Siri AI on iOS 27, and Screen security against AI on Android
items.what: Signal blocks screenshots so OS assistants like Siri AI and Gemini Intelligence can't read chats. Macs get no such protection.
items.why: If your app shows balances or statements, the same assistants can read them. Decide which of your screens block capture.

items.title: A House report counts the *Chinese models* in US apps
items.statLabel: Chinese model families DoorDash reported in use. Swapping an embedded one: up to 6 months
items.what: Airbnb runs Alibaba's Qwen for about 80,000 conversations a day. Cursor, whose Composer 2 is built on Moonshot's Kimi K2.5, is exploring a phase-out.
items.why: The committees want a model provenance standard. List every base model under your product, fine-tunes included, before a buyer asks.

items.title: AI judges grade stronger models *too kindly*
items.statLabel: points out of 1 that the best AI judge added to GPT-6 Astra's work, versus a human
items.what: METR's 20 Nov update: none of the eval tasks agents wrote were good enough to use, and its own container tests may overstate skill.
items.why: If an LLM grades your agent, calibrate it on human-scored samples, and again after every model upgrade.

courses.title: CS 329Z: Engineering AI Agents (Stanford)
courses.note: Diyi Yang, Michael Ryan and John Yang. 9 lecture videos so far, from RAG to multi-agent systems. Eval and safety slides are up.

courses.title: CMU AI Agents 2026: 13. Agentic Safety
courses.note: Graham Neubig's lecture for CMU 11-768, posted 16 Oct, from the course picked here on 6 Nov. Watch it before writing an allow list.

read: What it may *touch*: computer use has no sandbox, so the allow list is the fence. Who *checks* it: Amazon says automate the response, METR says calibrate the AI judge. Where its model *came from*: Congress wants it on record.
takeaway: Before an agent runs, write down what it may touch, who checks its work and where its model came from.
